subject: E-Commerce
title: Take Rates: The Marketplace Tax
description: A quick, practical guide to Take Rates: The Marketplace Tax.

hook.text: Amazon takes 30-45% of every sale when you add up fees, FBA costs, and advertising. Sellers keep barely half.

buildup.text: Take rate is the percentage a marketplace keeps from each transaction. It's the 'rent' for access to customers.

discovery.text: Etsy's take rate rose from 3.5% to 6.5% in a decade. Shopify charges 0% take rate, earning from subscriptions instead.

twist.text: Marketplaces raise take rates gradually. By the time sellers notice, they're too dependent on the platform to leave.

climax.text: Rising take rates are the hidden tax of marketplace dependence. Rent always goes up when the landlord has leverage.

punchline.text: 30-45% gone before profit. Marketplace fees start small and grow until sellers.

quiz.question: What is a marketplace 'take rate'?
options: The percentage of each sale the platform keeps in fees and commissions
